concepts: temporal extraction, frame comparison, concatenation, periodic oscillation
description: The input is not a single static grid but a short animation (a sequence of frames) showing:  - a uniform dark blue background  - an olive-green horizontal oval fixed center-top  - three purple triangular “pillars” aligned on the bottom  - a one-pixel-tall magenta stripe at the very bottom Over time the three purple pillars expand and contract in perfect sync (periodic oscillation), and the olive-green oval subtly brightens and dims in phase with them.
visual_elements: dark blue background filling entire frame
olive-green horizontal oval centered near the top
three purple triangular/pillar-like shapes aligned horizontally near the bottom
magenta stripe at the very bottom edge (one-pixel tall)
static_patterns: background color remains a uniform dark blue throughout
olive-green oval stays centered at the same vertical and horizontal position
three purple shapes retain their left-to-right order and baseline alignment
magenta bottom stripe remains at the bottom edge in every frame
dynamic_patterns: purple shapes cyclically change their vertical extent (grow taller, then shrink)
the three shapes animate in phase with each other (all expand, then all contract)
olive-green oval slightly changes its shading/brightness in sync with the pillars
animation loops continuously through the same sequence of frames
core_principles: periodic oscillation: repeated expansion and contraction over time
synchronization: multiple elements switching states simultaneously
state alternation: shapes alternate between two size/brightness states
cyclic repetition: the sequence of frames loops indefinitely
The most fundamental principle is that periodic oscillation drives the cyclic expansion and contraction of all shapes.
